recent_posts.title: How junior developers can build real skills while using AI tools
recent_posts.summary: Junior developers risk building shallow competence by relying on AI tools without understanding the code they ship. Five strategies are offered to counter this: learn fundamentals through books and studying experienced developers' code, study real-world system failures and postmortems, deliberately manufacture struggle by debugging manually before turning to AI, never commit code you can't explain, and prompt AI for multiple options with pros and cons to build genuine understanding. The core message is that developer value is shifting from shipping code to verifying and understanding it.

recent_posts.title: Why developers who ignore AI tools risk falling behind
recent_posts.summary: A software engineer turned manager shares a personal journey from AI skeptic to advocate, arguing that developers who don't adopt AI tools like Kiro and Claude Code are putting their careers at risk. The piece covers practical use cases including spec-driven development, brainstorming, Slack/document rewriting, and AI-powered project tracking. It also highlights the corporate angle: companies are actively rewarding AI adoption, and performance metrics tied to AI usage are already emerging. The core message is that the productivity baseline has shifted and non-adoption is no longer a neutral choice.

recent_posts.title: Understanding AI agents and how they enhance LLM capabilities
recent_posts.summary: AI agents enhance large language models by enabling multi-step reasoning and external tool integration. Unlike traditional LLMs that struggle with complex tasks, agents use a reasoning-action loop to break down problems into steps, plan approaches, and execute actions. Tools act as interfaces allowing agents to interact with external systems like databases, APIs, and file systems. Developers can use pre-built tools or create custom ones with simple annotations. Orchestration frameworks like AWS Strands Agents and LangGraph enable building agentic applications, with Strands offering a higher-level, beginner-friendly approach while LangGraph provides more granular control and advanced features.

recent_posts.title: Essential AWS services explained through building an e-commerce application
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive walkthrough of essential AWS services organized by function: networking (Route 53, CloudFront), storage (S3, EBS, EFS), compute (EC2, Lambda, ECS, Fargate), databases (RDS, DynamoDB, Aurora), security (WAF, Cognito, Certificate Manager), AI/ML (Bedrock, SageMaker), messaging (SNS, SQS, EventBridge), analytics (Athena, EMR, Redshift), monitoring (CloudWatch, X-Ray), and CI/CD (CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CodePipeline). Uses an e-commerce application as a practical example to demonstrate how these services integrate to build production systems.

recent_posts.title: Creating handdrawn videos with Arnote and drawing tablets
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of Arnote, an open-source note-taking application built in Rust that works across Linux, macOS, and Windows. The guide covers customizing the canvas appearance (removing grid lines, changing background colors), demonstrates the drawing smoothing algorithm, and highlights a unique feature for expanding canvas space vertically. Also includes a recommendation for the Wacom Intuos medium tablet as the preferred drawing hardware for creating handwritten content.

recent_posts.title: Using AWS MCP to manage cloud resources with natural language
recent_posts.summary: AWS MCP (Model Context Protocol) enables developers to interact with AWS resources using natural language through AI-powered IDEs like Cursor. The tool allows LLMs to execute AWS CLI commands directly, enabling operations like creating S3 buckets, listing resources, and managing infrastructure through conversational prompts. The system works by translating natural language requests into AWS CLI commands that run against your configured AWS credentials. Key considerations include using restrictive IAM policies for security, providing specific instructions for better results, and leveraging the tool to generate Infrastructure as Code templates after manual operations.

recent_posts.title: AWS fundamentals for beginners
recent_posts.summary: AWS revolutionized computing by replacing expensive on-premises server rooms with scalable cloud infrastructure. The platform offers over 250 services across categories like storage (S3), compute (EC2), and databases (DynamoDB) that work together to build powerful applications. AWS operates through regions worldwide for low latency and availability zones within each region for high availability and disaster recovery. This pay-as-you-go model enables companies to focus on their core business instead of managing hardware infrastructure.
